title: `Pot.join` / `Jug.file` — `rho` freshness requirement enables griefing via forced `drip` ordering
impact: `Pot.join` requires `now == rho` exactly. Since `drip()` sets `rho = now`, any `join` in a later block reverts until someone calls `drip()`. An attacker can front-run `join` by calling `drip()` in the same block *after* `rho` was set in a prior block — no, `drip` sets `rho = now` so `join` in the *same block* succeeds. The real risk: if `drip()` is not called, `join` is blocked for users in every subsequent block, and `Pot.file("dsr", ...)` also requires `now == rho`, so governance cannot change the DSR until a `drip` lands. This is a liveness/griefing surface (anyone can `drip`, so severity is bounded), but combined with a `Vat`/RPC outage it blocks user deposits.
